summary: Sanya fits warm-weather coastal travel centered on beach pacing, resort-adjacent dining, sea views, and low-pressure day structure.
transport_notes: Keep each day focused on one bay or one coastal zone to avoid spending too much time in transit.
Beach, island, and shopping-resort areas should be paired carefully because cross-bay movement can eat into the day.
Evenings work best around bayfront promenades, resort dining areas, or walkable market streets.

budget_notes.low: Use public beach areas, simple seafood or local-food streets, and scenic walks over heavy attraction stacking.
budget_notes.medium: Combine one bay-area stop, one scenic public space, and one stronger evening dining area each day.
budget_notes.high: Lean into slower comfort pacing, better sea-view dining, and fewer transfers between coastal zones.

trip_type_notes.student: Student plans in Sanya should emphasize scenic public beaches, simple local food, and casual youth-friendly sea-city rhythm.
trip_type_notes.solo: Solo plans should feel calm, sunlit, and easy to adapt around coastlines and personal pacing.
trip_type_notes.couple: Couple plans should highlight sunset, sea breeze, and more intimate beach-to-dinner transitions.
trip_type_notes.family: Family plans should focus on convenient beach access, broad public spaces, and easy dining without overmovement.
